help.metaDescription: What HilaTech Knowledge Studio does and how to use it: asking questions, reading answers and sources, the demo and the workspace.
help.title: How to use Knowledge Studio
help.lead: Knowledge Studio answers questions from your own documents and shows the passage behind every statement. This page explains what it does and how to use it.

what.title: What Knowledge Studio does
paragraphs: You give it documents: policies, handbooks, catalogs, procedures. You ask a question in plain language. It finds the passages that answer the question, writes a short answer from them, and marks each statement with the source it came from.
It answers only from the documents in the library. It does not use general knowledge from the internet, and when the documents do not cover a question it says so instead of guessing.

how.title: How it works
paragraphs: Four things happen between a file and an answer.
points: Reading. Each document is read and split into short passages. Page numbers and headings are kept.
Indexing. Every passage is stored by its meaning, so a question can find it even when it uses different words, or a different language.
Retrieving. When you ask, the passages closest in meaning to your question are found. Only passages from your own organization are searched.
Answering. The answer is written from those passages only, and each statement carries a numbered citation.

demo.title: Trying the demo
paragraphs: The demo needs no account. It holds twelve documents of Northstar Business Services, a fictional company: six in English and the same six in Hebrew.
points: Open the demo from the menu.
Choose one of the suggested questions, or type your own in the box at the bottom and press Enter.
Read the answer, then select a citation number to see the passage it relies on.
Ask another question in the same conversation, or start again with New chat. Each question is answered on its own, so write it in full.

asking.title: Asking good questions
points: Ask the way you would ask a colleague: “Who approves a refund above $400?”
Ask one thing at a time. Two questions in one sentence work, but separate questions are easier to check.
Name the plan, product or policy you mean when several are similar.
You can ask in Hebrew or in English, whatever language the document is written in.
A question can be up to 2,000 characters.

reading.title: Reading an answer
points: Citation numbers. The small number after a statement points to its source. Select it to open the evidence panel.
Evidence panel. It shows the document, the page and the passage, with the quoted part highlighted. The answer is a summary of that passage, so the passage is what to rely on.
Sources. The button under the answer lists every source the answer used.
Copy answer. Copies the text of the answer.
An answer without any citation is marked as unchecked. Treat it with caution.

noAnswer.title: When there is no answer
paragraphs: If the documents do not contain the information, the reply is: “I couldn't find reliable information about that in the available documents.” This is the intended behaviour. It means the library has no passage that supports an answer, not that something is broken.
If you expected an answer, check that the document is in the library and shows as Ready, and try naming the subject more specifically.

languages.title: Languages and display
points: The site is available in English and in Hebrew. Use the language switch in the header; Hebrew is shown right to left.
Answers come in the language of the question.
The sun and moon button switches between the light and the dark theme.

limits.title: Limits of the public demo
paragraphs: The demo is open to everyone, so it is limited.
points: 15 questions per visitor session.
4 questions per minute from one address.
300 questions per day for all visitors together.
Documents cannot be uploaded in the demo, and the sample documents cannot be changed.
Northstar Business Services and everything in its documents are invented.

workspace.title: The workspace, for signed-in teams
paragraphs: A signed-in organization gets a private workspace with its own library. To open an account, sign up on the sign-up page and confirm your email address with the link we send to it.
points: Library. Upload PDF, Word (.docx), text or Markdown files, up to 20 MB each. Scanned PDF pages are read by automatic text recognition where it is switched on, with a page limit; text read from a scan can contain mistakes.
Status. A document moves through Waiting and Processing to Ready. Only Ready documents are used in answers. A Failed document shows the reason and can be retried.
Ask. Works like the demo, over your own documents, and keeps your conversations in the side panel.
Deleting a document removes it and its indexed text. Earlier answers keep their wording, and their citations to it are marked as removed.
Roles. Owners and admins manage documents and members; members ask questions.

privacy.title: Privacy and trust
points: Documents are kept in private storage and are used only to answer questions inside their own organization.
Every organization is separate. People see only the documents of the organization they belong to.
Text inside a document is treated as content, never as an instruction to the assistant.
An answer is a summary. For a decision that matters, read the cited passage.

faq.title: Common questions
points: Why did it cite the English document when I asked in Hebrew, or the other way round? In the demo every document exists in both languages with the same content, and either edition can support the answer.
Can it answer from two documents at once? Yes. Each statement cites its own source.
Does it remember earlier questions? No. Each question is answered on its own, even inside one conversation, so write every question in full.
Why was my question refused? Either the documents do not cover it, or a demo limit was reached. The message says which.
